evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: Not asked. Rep moved directly into logistics probing after asking about property type without surfacing customer concerns first.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — no concerns were raised by the customer; they stated only 'we just have to be done tomorrow at later tomorrow morning,' a deadline not a concern.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Not addressed. Rep offered a single time window (8:30 AM to 9:00 AM) without discussing date flexibility or cheaper alternative days.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Weak. Rep asked 'So should I confirm now you're booking for tomorrow?' without first stating rate lock or no-deposit commitment. Customer declined: 'Do you know let me make another couple of calls and I'll call you back, okay?'

top_strength: Jeline gathered comprehensive logistics details (addresses, floor level, access, furniture inventory, property type and layout) and asked the box-count question, building an estimate on solid information.
coaching_note: Lead with the two-concerns question before probing logistics, deliver both promises (On-Time Guarantee and No Worries Damage Coverage) with permission lead-in, and anchor the estimate to the customer's prep level before asking for the business — rate lock and no-deposit must come before the ask itself, never after.
